ALP: Alkaline phosphatase (U/L), an enzyme marker for liver, bone, or intestinal function, elevated in hepatobiliary disease or bone disorders.
ALT: Alanine aminotransferase (U/L), a liver-specific enzyme marker for hepatocellular injury, commonly elevated in hepatitis or drug-induced liver damage.
AST: Aspartate aminotransferase (U/L), an enzyme marker for liver and muscle damage, elevated in hepatic disease, myocardial infarction, or skeletal muscle injury.
Albumin: Serum albumin (g/dL), a protein marker of nutritional status and liver synthetic function, decreased in malnutrition, liver disease, or nephrotic syndrome.
Albumin 25%: 25% albumin solution (mL), a concentrated colloid fluid for volume expansion and treatment of hypoalbuminemia in critically ill patients.
Albumin 5%: 5% albumin solution (mL), a colloid fluid for volume expansion and plasma protein replacement in hypovolemia or hypoalbuminemia.
Amiodarone: Amiodarone dosage (mg), a class III antiarrhythmic medication for treatment of ventricular and supraventricular arrhythmias.
Anion Gap: Anion gap (mEq/L), calculated as (Na+ - Cl- - HCO3-), a marker of metabolic acidosis etiology, elevated in lactic acidosis, ketoacidosis, or toxic ingestions.
BUN: Blood urea nitrogen (mg/dL), a marker of kidney function and protein metabolism, elevated in renal failure, dehydration, or high protein intake.
Base Excess: Base excess (mEq/L), an indicator of metabolic acid-base imbalance, negative in metabolic acidosis and positive in metabolic alkalosis.
Basophils: Basophil count (cells/mm³), a type of white blood cell involved in allergic reactions and inflammation, elevated in hypersensitivity or myeloproliferative disorders.
Bicarbonate: Serum bicarbonate (mEq/L), a key component of acid-base balance, decreased in metabolic acidosis or increased in metabolic alkalosis.
Bilirubin (Direct): Direct bilirubin (mg/dL), a marker of liver function and biliary obstruction, elevated in cholestasis or hepatocellular disease.
Bilirubin (Indirect): Indirect bilirubin (mg/dL), a marker of hemolysis and liver conjugation function, elevated in hemolytic anemia or Gilbert syndrome.
Bilirubin (Total): Total bilirubin (mg/dL), a marker of liver function and hemolysis, elevated in hepatobiliary disease, hemolytic anemia, or Gilbert syndrome.
CRR: Capillary refill rate (seconds), a clinical indicator of peripheral perfusion and circulatory status, prolonged in shock or peripheral vascular disease.
Calcium Free: Ionized calcium (mg/dL), the biologically active form of calcium in blood, critical for cardiac function, muscle contraction, and coagulation.
Calcium Gluconate: Calcium gluconate dosage (mEq or mg), an intravenous calcium supplement for hypocalcemia, hyperkalemia, or calcium channel blocker overdose.
Calcium Total: Total serum calcium (mg/dL), an electrolyte essential for bone health, muscle contraction, nerve function, and blood clotting.
Cefazolin: Cefazolin dosage (mg), a first-generation cephalosporin antibiotic for surgical prophylaxis and treatment of gram-positive bacterial infections.
Chest Tube: Chest tube drainage output (mL), measures pleural fluid or air removal, indicator of hemothorax, pneumothorax, or pleural effusion resolution.
Chloride: Serum chloride (mEq/L), an electrolyte important for fluid balance and acid-base status, abnormal in dehydration or metabolic alkalosis.
Colloid: Colloid fluid administration (mL), includes albumin or synthetic colloids for volume expansion in hypovolemia or shock.
Creatinine Blood: Serum creatinine (mg/dL), a critical marker of kidney function reflecting glomerular filtration rate, elevated in acute or chronic renal failure.
Creatinine Urine: Urine creatinine (mg/dL), used to calculate creatinine clearance and assess kidney function, also used to validate urine sample adequacy.
D5W: Dextrose 5% in water (mL), an intravenous fluid providing free water and calories, used for hydration and hypoglycemia treatment.
DBP: Diastolic blood pressure (mmHg), arterial pressure during cardiac relaxation phase, indicator of peripheral vascular resistance.
Dextrose Other: Other dextrose-containing intravenous fluids (mL), various concentrations for hydration, calorie supply, or medication dilution.
Dopamine: Dopamine dosage (mcg/kg/min), a vasoactive medication for blood pressure support and cardiac output enhancement in shock states.
EBL: Estimated blood loss (mL), a clinical marker of hemorrhage severity during surgery or trauma, guides transfusion decisions.
Emesis: Emesis volume (mL), measures vomiting output, indicator of nausea severity, gastrointestinal obstruction, or medication side effects.
Eoisinophils: Eosinophil count (cells/mm³), a type of white blood cell involved in allergic reactions and parasitic infections, elevated in asthma or eosinophilic disorders.
Epinephrine: Epinephrine dosage (mcg/min), a potent vasopressor and bronchodilator for cardiac arrest, anaphylaxis, and severe hypotension.
Famotidine: Famotidine dosage (mg), an H2-receptor antagonist for gastric acid suppression, stress ulcer prophylaxis, and GERD treatment.
Fentanyl: Fentanyl dosage (mcg), a potent synthetic opioid analgesic for pain management and sedation in critically ill patients.
FiO2: Fraction of inspired oxygen (%), the percentage of oxygen in inhaled air delivered to the patient, critical parameter for ventilation management.
Fiber: Dietary fiber intake (grams), indicator of nutritional intake and gastrointestinal health, important for enteral nutrition management.
Free Water: Free water administration (mL), hypotonic fluid for correcting hypernatremia or providing maintenance fluid requirements.
Fresh Frozen Plasma: Fresh frozen plasma transfusion (mL), a blood product containing coagulation factors for treatment of coagulopathy or massive transfusion.
Furosemide: Furosemide dosage (mg), a loop diuretic for treatment of fluid overload, pulmonary edema, and acute kidney injury.
GCS_eye: Glasgow Coma Scale eye opening response (1-4), assesses neurological function: 4=spontaneous, 3=to voice, 2=to pain, 1=none.
GCS_motor: Glasgow Coma Scale motor response (1-6), assesses neurological motor function: 6=obeys commands, 5=localizes pain, 4=withdraws, 3=flexion, 2=extension, 1=none.
GCS_verbal: Glasgow Coma Scale verbal response (1-5), assesses neurological verbal function: 5=oriented, 4=confused, 3=inappropriate, 2=incomprehensible, 1=none.
GT Flush: Gastric tube flush volume (mL), fluid used to maintain gastric tube patency and assess tube placement.
Gastric: Gastric output volume (mL), measures gastric secretions or residual, indicator of gastrointestinal function and feeding tolerance.
Gastric Meds: Gastric medications administration, includes proton pump inhibitors, H2 blockers, or antacids for gastric acid suppression and ulcer prophylaxis.
Glucose (Blood): Blood glucose from fingerstick (mg/dL), point-of-care measurement for rapid glucose monitoring in diabetes management.
Glucose (Serum): Serum glucose from venous sample (mg/dL), laboratory measurement of blood glucose for diabetes diagnosis and monitoring.
Glucose (Whole Blood): Whole blood glucose (mg/dL), glucose measurement from arterial or venous blood gas sample.
HR: Heart rate (beats per minute), a vital sign reflecting cardiac activity and autonomic function, abnormal in arrhythmias, shock, or fever.
Half Normal Saline: 0.45% sodium chloride solution (mL), a hypotonic intravenous fluid for free water replacement and hypernatremia correction.
Hct: Hematocrit (%), the percentage of red blood cells in total blood volume, decreased in anemia or increased in polycythemia or dehydration.
Heparin: Heparin dosage (units), an anticoagulant for prevention and treatment of venous thromboembolism and during cardiac procedures.
Hgb: Hemoglobin (g/dL), the oxygen-carrying protein in red blood cells, decreased in anemia or blood loss, critical for oxygen delivery assessment.
Hydralazine: Hydralazine dosage (mg), a direct vasodilator for treatment of hypertensive emergencies and heart failure.
Hydromorphone: Hydromorphone dosage (mg), a potent opioid analgesic for moderate to severe pain management in critically ill patients.
INR: International normalized ratio, a standardized measure of blood clotting tendency for warfarin monitoring and coagulopathy assessment.
Insulin Humalog: Insulin lispro (Humalog) dosage (units), a rapid-acting insulin analog for prandial blood glucose control.
Insulin NPH: NPH insulin dosage (units), an intermediate-acting insulin for basal blood glucose control in diabetes management.
Insulin Regular: Regular insulin dosage (units), a short-acting insulin for blood glucose control and hyperkalemia treatment.
Insulin largine: Insulin glargine (Lantus) dosage (units), a long-acting insulin analog for basal blood glucose control.
Intubated: Intubation status (0/1), indicates whether the patient has an endotracheal tube for mechanical ventilation support.
Jackson-Pratt: Jackson-Pratt drain output (mL), measures surgical site drainage, indicator of postoperative bleeding or fluid accumulation.
KCl: Potassium chloride infusion (mEq), an electrolyte supplement for prevention and treatment of hypokalemia.
KCl (Bolus): Potassium chloride bolus dosage (mEq), rapid potassium replacement for severe hypokalemia with cardiac monitoring.
LDH: Lactate dehydrogenase (U/L), an enzyme marker of tissue damage in liver, muscle, blood cells, or malignancy.
Lactate: Blood lactate (mmol/L), a marker of tissue hypoxia and anaerobic metabolism, elevated in sepsis, shock, or tissue hypoperfusion.
Lactated Ringers: Lactated Ringer's solution (mL), a balanced crystalloid fluid containing lactate, sodium, potassium, calcium, and chloride for resuscitation.
Lorazepam: Lorazepam dosage (mg), a benzodiazepine for sedation, anxiety, seizure control, and alcohol withdrawal management.
Lymphocytes: Lymphocyte percentage (%), a type of white blood cell involved in adaptive immune response, decreased in immunosuppression or viral infections.
Lymphocytes (Absolute): Absolute lymphocyte count (cells/mm³), marker of immune function, decreased in HIV, chemotherapy, or severe infections.
MBP: Mean blood pressure (mmHg), the average arterial pressure over a cardiac cycle, critical for assessing organ perfusion.
MCH: Mean corpuscular hemoglobin (pg), the average amount of hemoglobin per red blood cell, indicator of anemia type.
MCHC: Mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (g/dL), the average concentration of hemoglobin in red blood cells.
MCV: Mean corpuscular volume (fL), the average size of red blood cells, indicator of anemia type (microcytic, normocytic, macrocytic).
Magnesium: Serum magnesium (mg/dL), an electrolyte vital for neuromuscular function, cardiac rhythm, and enzyme activity, deficiency can cause arrhythmias.
Magnesium Sulfate (Bolus): Magnesium sulfate bolus dosage (g), for acute magnesium replacement, torsades de pointes, or eclampsia treatment.
Magnesium Sulphate: Magnesium sulfate infusion (g), an electrolyte supplement for hypomagnesemia and seizure prophylaxis in preeclampsia.
Metoprolol: Metoprolol dosage (mg), a beta-blocker for heart rate control, hypertension, and acute coronary syndrome management.
Midazolam: Midazolam dosage (mg), a short-acting benzodiazepine for sedation, procedural anxiolysis, and seizure control.
Milrinone: Milrinone dosage (mcg/kg/min), a phosphodiesterase inhibitor inotrope for acute decompensated heart failure management.
Monocytes: Monocyte count (cells/mm³), a type of white blood cell involved in immune response and inflammation, elevated in chronic infections.
Morphine Sulfate: Morphine sulfate dosage (mg), an opioid analgesic for moderate to severe pain management and acute pulmonary edema.
Neosynephrine: Phenylephrine (Neosynephrine) dosage (mcg/min), a pure alpha-agonist vasopressor for hypotension without cardiac depression.
Neutrophils: Neutrophil count (cells/mm³), a type of white blood cell central to immune defense against bacterial infections, decreased in neutropenia.
Nitroglycerine: Nitroglycerin dosage (mcg/min), a vasodilator for angina, acute coronary syndrome, and hypertensive emergency management.
Nitroprusside: Sodium nitroprusside dosage (mcg/kg/min), a potent vasodilator for hypertensive emergencies and acute heart failure.
Norepinephrine: Norepinephrine dosage (mcg/min), a potent vasopressor for septic shock and severe hypotension management.
Normal Saline: 0.9% sodium chloride solution (mL), an isotonic crystalloid fluid for volume resuscitation and medication dilution.
O2 Saturation: Oxygen saturation (%), the percentage of hemoglobin bound to oxygen, measured by pulse oximetry or arterial blood gas.
OR/PACU Crystalloid: Operating room/post-anesthesia care unit crystalloid fluid (mL), intraoperative and postoperative fluid administration.
PCO2: Partial pressure of carbon dioxide in blood (mmHg), reflects respiratory acid-base balance and ventilation adequacy.
PO intake: Oral (PO) intake volume (mL), measures oral fluid and nutrient intake, indicator of nutritional and hydration status.
PO2: Partial pressure of oxygen in blood (mmHg), a key indicator of oxygenation status and pulmonary gas exchange efficiency.
PT: Prothrombin time (seconds), a coagulation marker measuring extrinsic pathway function, prolonged in warfarin therapy or liver disease.
PTT: Partial thromboplastin time (seconds), a coagulation marker measuring intrinsic pathway function, prolonged in heparin therapy.
Packed RBC: Packed red blood cell transfusion (units or mL), a blood product for treatment of anemia or acute blood loss.
Pantoprazole: Pantoprazole dosage (mg), a proton pump inhibitor for gastric acid suppression, stress ulcer prophylaxis, and GERD treatment.
Phosphate: Serum phosphate (mg/dL), an electrolyte important for bone health, energy metabolism, and cell function, abnormal in renal failure.
Piggyback: Piggyback intravenous medication (mL), a secondary infusion method for delivering medications via existing IV line.
Piperacillin: Piperacillin dosage (g), a broad-spectrum beta-lactam antibiotic often combined with tazobactam for serious bacterial infections.
Platelet Count: Platelet count (cells/mm³), a marker of blood clotting ability, decreased in thrombocytopenia or increased in reactive thrombocytosis.
Potassium: Serum potassium (mEq/L), a critical electrolyte for cardiac rhythm, muscle contraction, and nerve function.
Pre-admission Intake: Pre-admission fluid intake (mL), baseline fluid intake before hospital admission for fluid balance assessment.
Pre-admission Output: Pre-admission urine output (mL), baseline urine output before hospital admission for renal function reference.
Propofol: Propofol dosage (mcg/kg/min), an intravenous sedative-hypnotic agent for procedural sedation and ICU sedation.
RBC: Red blood cell count (cells/mm³), a marker of oxygen-carrying capacity, decreased in anemia or increased in polycythemia.
RDW: Red cell distribution width (%), measures variation in red blood cell size, elevated in iron deficiency anemia or mixed anemias.
RR: Respiratory rate (breaths per minute), a vital sign reflecting pulmonary function and respiratory drive.
Residual: Gastric residual volume (mL), measures undigested feeding in stomach, indicator of feeding tolerance and gastroparesis.
SBP: Systolic blood pressure (mmHg), arterial pressure during cardiac contraction phase, indicator of cardiac output and vascular tone.
SG Urine: Urine specific gravity (1.001-1.030), a measure of urine concentration reflecting hydration status and kidney concentrating ability.
Sodium: Serum sodium (mEq/L), a critical electrolyte for fluid balance, nerve conduction, and muscle function.
Solution: Intravenous solution administration (mL), general category for various IV fluids used for hydration and medication delivery.
Sterile Water: Sterile water administration (mL), used for medication dilution, wound irrigation, or humidification.
Stool: Stool output (mL or frequency), indicator of gastrointestinal function, hydration status, and diarrhea severity.
TPN: Total parenteral nutrition (mL/hour), intravenous nutrient solution for patients unable to receive enteral nutrition.
Temperature: Body temperature (°C or °F), a vital sign reflecting thermoregulation, elevated in infection, inflammation, or hyperthermia.
Total CO2: Total carbon dioxide (mEq/L), reflects bicarbonate and dissolved CO2, an indicator of acid-base balance.
Ultrafiltrate: Ultrafiltrate volume (mL), fluid removed during continuous renal replacement therapy or dialysis.
Unknown: Unknown or unclassified clinical variable, may represent miscellaneous measurements or data entry errors.
Urine: Urine output (mL/hour or mL/day), an indicator of renal function and hydration status, decreased in acute kidney injury.
Vacomycin: Vancomycin dosage (mg), a glycopeptide antibiotic for serious gram-positive infections including MRSA and C. difficile.
Vasopressin: Vasopressin dosage (units/hour), an antidiuretic hormone used as a vasopressor in septic shock and diabetes insipidus.
WBC: White blood cell count (cells/mm³), a marker of immune response and infection, elevated in bacterial infection or leukemia.
pH Blood: Blood pH value (7.35-7.45 normal range), an indicator of acid-base balance status in respiratory or metabolic disorders.
pH Urine: Urine pH (4.5-8.0 normal range), an indicator of urinary tract acid-base balance, kidney stone risk, and urinary tract infection.
